subject: general
question: What is the third stage (after larva) in the lifecycle of a butterfly called?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Pupa.**__

__
 
• The third stage in the lifecycle of a butterfly is called **Pupa**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• During the third stage, the caterpillar forms a **chrysalis (or pupa) **which is usually brown or green so it is camouflaged. This is the transformation stage, when it starts to grow wings.
 
• **A pupa** is the life stage of some insects undergoing transformation between immature and mature stages. Insects that go through a pupal stage are holometabolous: they go through four distinct stages in their life cycle, the stages thereof being egg, larva, pupa, and imago
 
• A pupa forms following the completion of larval development and contains the metamorphosing adult.
 
• During the stage, the caterpillar forms a** protective chrysalis** that protects it from the outside world while allowing it to undergo important changes. 

 The caterpillar will stay in this stage for about **a week. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The life cycle of a butterfly is truly amazing. Butterflies have four life stages,** the egg, the larva (caterpillar), the pupa (chrysalis), and the adult butterfly.**
 
• Each of the four stages is very unique to individual species of butterflies which is part of what makes watching and raising butterflies so much fun.
 
• The adult butterfly **first lays her eggs** safely on a leaf. Depending on the type of butterfly, she may lay just one egg, dozens of eggs, or up to hundreds of eggs at once.
 
• The egg begins to hatch and a caterpillar is revealed. This caterpillar is known as the **larva stag**e. The caterpillar crawls out of the egg and immediately begins to start eating.
 
• After about a week later, the caterpillar is ready to emerge from its chrysalis and enter the** fourth stage** of the life cycle.
